messages:
acme_integration_dev: Hey team — after the model upgrade yesterday our webhook JSON parser started failing. Nested objects are coming back as escaped strings, e.g. address field is a single string with \"{\"street\":\"1 Main\",\"city\":\"SF\"}\". This breaks our downstream consumer.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a request_id and the model alias you hit? Any sample input + output helps.

acme_integration_dev: request_id=req_01GXY9Z3, model=redwood-instruct-v4.1, timestamp=2024-03-02T14:22:31Z. Minimal prompt attached below. Repro is 100% for us.

acme_integration_dev: ```
user_prompt: \"Return contact info in JSON with nested address object\"
expected: {\"name\":\"Alice\", \"contact\": {\"phone\":\"555-1234\", \"address\": {\"street\":\"1 Main\", \"city\":\"SF\"}}}
actual: {\"name\":\"Alice\", \"contact\": {\"phone\":\"555-1234\", \"address\": \"{\\\"street\\\":\\\"1 Main\\\",\\\"city\\\":\\\"SF\\\"}\"}}
```

raj_engineer: Thanks — I see the request in logs. Model variant redwood-instruct-v4.1 was part of yesterday's canary rollout (canary-id: canary-20240302-3). We have a heuristic that flattens inferred nested schema for some generator configs; looks like it triggered and serialized the object to a string.

raj_engineer: Can you confirm if you're using structured_output=true or the json_mode flag in your API call? That changes how we post-process completions.

acme_integration_dev: We set json_mode=true and schema={contact: {address: object}}. Worked fine before the upgrade. No changes on our side.

olivia_prod: tagging eng-ml — raj is on it. Initial hypothesis: a tokenizer/kernel change in v4.1 caused the model to output braces without a clear token boundary and the post-processor interpreted it as plain text, then serialized it instead of merging. I'll try to repro locally with the exact prompt + model alias.

raj_engineer: Repro steps I'm running: 1) call /generate with model=redwood-instruct-v4.1 json_mode=true schema provided; 2) capture raw model stream; 3) apply postprocess JSON unwrapping. Early run shows raw stream contains \"address\": \"{...}\" rather than nested braces.

raj_engineer: Quick mitigation: rolling back canary to v4.0 for affected capacity. Deploy bot will post status. If you need immediate unblock, switch model param to redwood-instruct-v4.0 or set json_mode=false and parse text yourself.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: canary-20240302-3 -> revert to redwood-instruct-v4.0 on pool-7. ETA ~8m.

maria_support: I've informed the customer about rollback and recommended switching to v4.0 while we investigate. Asking for their SLA impact so we can prioritize.

acme_integration_dev: Thanks, rollback helped — switching to v4.0 fixed the nested object output. Impact: production webhook failures for ~30min, some orders delayed. We need a postmortem and a plan to prevent schema drift on model swaps.

raj_engineer: Understood. Next steps: 1) capture more raw streams for failing cases, 2) add an assert in postprocessor that fails loudly instead of serializing when schema expects object, 3) add canary tests for json_mode edge-cases before rollout. I'll open an internal ticket and link logs + request ids.

olivia_prod: Also adding a regression test in the eval harness for nested objects and for serializers to avoid silent conversions.

maria_support: I'll schedule a customer-facing postmortem and share timeline. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

acme_integration_dev: Appreciated — please include exact rollback time and the canary id in the PM.

raj_engineer: Will do. Ticket: INF-4021. Attaching collected raw stream snippet to the ticket.

maria_support: thread closed after rollback confirmation, continuing in INF-4021 for engineering follow-up.
